data.intro: In Rakhigarhi, women are building on existing knowledge and ways of making. Through practice and creative exchange, they are developing skills, individual expression and new pathways to livelihood.

data.body_html:
Ways of choosing materials, judging a form or working with colour are often learned through watching, doing and making alongside others.

USP brings women in Rakhigarhi together with artists, designers and craft practitioners to build on this knowledge. Together, they test and adapt new materials, techniques and ideas, developing work rooted in the place and shaped by the women involved.
data.heading: Not everything we know is formally taught.

data.body_html: Three crafts form the starting point of the initiative. Each brings its own materials, techniques and possibilities for colour, pattern and form.
data.heading: Basket Making. Papier-Mâché. Dhurrie Weaving.

data.body_html: Basket making draws on skills and ways of working already present within the community. Through the initiative, women are exploring new combinations of colour, pattern and form while developing the consistency and finish of the work.
data.heading: Tradition carried forward through colour, pattern and form.

data.body_html: Papier-mâché introduces a different material and process into the initiative. Women are experimenting with form, surface and decoration, developing objects that combine individual expression with the visual language emerging from the group.
data.heading: A new material. A new direction.

media.alt: Small handmade figures, bowls and other objects displayed on the ground.
media.caption: Small handmade figures and bowls on display.

data.body_html: The patterns and motifs woven into the dhurries draw on designs passed down through generations within the community. Women use these as a starting point for new combinations of colour and composition—carrying local textile knowledge into the work being created today.
data.heading: Textile knowledge carried forward through pattern and composition.

media.alt: A framed textile wall hanging with animal and bird motifs against a brick wall.
media.caption: A textile wall hanging with animal and bird motifs.

data.body_html:
The Craft Centre within the Rakhigarhi Haveli and Chaupal will give the initiative a shared home—a place for women to work together, develop designs and techniques, share knowledge and build consistency in what they produce.

Visitors will be able to encounter the work and understand the people, materials, and processes behind it.
data.heading: A Place for the Work to Continue.

data.body_html:
As baskets, papier-mâché and dhurries develop into products with wider appeal and economic value, they can create opportunities for women to earn.

Women are also contributing ideas, developing products and becoming more involved in decisions about how the initiative grows.

As the work gains value, so do the opportunities around it.
data.heading: Creating Value Through Craft.

data.aside: Rakhigarhi is known for its extraordinary past. The ambition is to make what is created here part of its future.
data.body_html:
The work begins in Rakhigarhi, with the ambition to reach wider audiences through collections, creative collaborations, and partnerships.

The aim is for craft from Rakhigarhi to be recognised for its quality, character and originality—with women increasingly shaping what is created and where it goes next.
data.heading: From Rakhigarhi, Outwards.
